subject: QBR: Runway decision matrix & batching/caching tradeoffs
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR: Runway decision matrix & batching/caching tradeoffs

Team — attaching the decision matrix (qbr_runway_decision_matrix.xlsx) and supporting GPU econ summary (gpu_econ_runway.pdf). This thread is the single source for the leadership ask for Tuesday's QBR. TL;DR: we need a direction on runway allocation and an approval on the recommended batching/caching aggressiveness so the infra and product teams can lock config and rollout windows before the QBR deck is finalized.

Key questions for decision:
- Runway allocation: commit an additional 120 dedicated slots for Reserved (paid) to hedge enterprise renewals, or keep as burst-only and absorb risk? (Decision options A/B/C in the matrix)
- Batching / KV-cache aggressiveness: pick conservative (A), balanced (B), or aggressive (C). Effects are summarized on tab "Econ Impact".
- GPU spend target for next quarter (high-level number) — do we accept the proposed 12% increase to secure latency SLO headroom?

What I need by EOD: your preferred option (A/B/C) and any hard constraints (e.g., we cannot increase spend beyond X). If you disagree with the wording in the matrix, call it out inline — I will incorporate edits and produce the final QBR slide.

Notes: the matrix includes simulated utilization curves across PLG-hosted traffic vs enterprise (Stratton Health pilot is the sentinel enterprise workload). Numbers assume current quantization and slot sizing. Karthik — I flagged the simulation tabs for you to sanity-check. Markus — flagged the latency SLO rows for your input.

Thanks,
Maya Srinivasan
Head of Infrastructure Economics
Redwood Inference

Attachments: qbr_runway_decision_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), gpu_econ_runway.pdf (summary)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: Runway decision matrix & batching/caching tradeoffs

On Mon, Jul 9, 2028 at 9:12 AM Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — attaching the decision matrix ...

Quick read — I prefer option B (balanced). Rationale: it preserves enterprise latency headroom while still unlocking ~8–10% unit-cost savings from smarter batching + prefix caching for PLG traffic. A couple of requests before I lock the simulation:
- Can we run the same matrix with the KV-cache invalidation rate set to +15% (simulates churn spikes)? I want to ensure B still holds when we lose cached prefixes.
- Please include a short-run simulation (72h burst) with the proposed slot mix to check tail latency. I'll run that against staging tomorrow and post results.

If you need a quick call today, I'm free 11:30–12:15.

—Karthik
VP, Serving Orchestration
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jul 2028 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: Runway decision matrix & batching/caching tradeoffs

On Mon, Jul 9, 2028 at 10:03 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick read — I prefer option B ...

I looked through the latency rows for the enterprise buckets. For Stratton Health (they're on the pilot), we have zero tolerance for p95 regressions above 50ms over baseline. Given we still have some open optimization work on the attention kernel for long prompts, I'm inclined to ask leadership to accept a split approach:
- Approve Option A for enterprise/reserved pools (conservative config, no aggressive batching)
- Approve Option B experiment for hosted/PLG traffic with a canary and 2-week burn and explicit rollback windows

I've attached a short note (markus_latency_note.txt) that lists 3 latency gates we should not cross before we declare safety for enterprise migration.

If leadership is comfortable with the split approach, we can present both the conservative runway allocation (enterprise) and the upside from the PLG experiments in the QBR — it's more defensible.

Markus Klein
VP, Reliability & SRE
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Geller <emma@strattonhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jul 2028 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: Runway decision matrix & batching/caching tradeoffs

Thanks — great discussion. Consolidating decisions and action items so the QBR slide deck can be finalized.

Leadership decision (approved):
- Runway allocation: commit an extra 80 dedicated slots immediately for Reserved / Enterprise (partial hedge). We will keep an additional 40 slots as burst-only contingency for the quarter (this is compromise between A and B in the matrix).
- Batching / KV-cache policy: split approach approved. Option A (conservative) for enterprise/reserved pools; Option B (balanced) as a controlled experiment for hosted/PLG traffic with a 2-week burn and explicit rollback criteria.
- GPU spend: approve up to an 8% increase vs baseline for the quarter to cover slot commitments + two-week experiment. Any further increases require escalation.

Action items (owners & deadlines):
- Karthik: run KV-cache churn sensitivity sim (+15%) and 72h burst tail-latency run; share numbers by EOD Tuesday.
- Markus: own enterprise latency gates and coordinate with Stratton Health (Emma) on pilot windows; provide gating checklist by Wednesday.
- Maya: update QBR deck (qbr_final_action_items.pdf) and decision matrix to reflect split approach; finalize slides by Thursday COB.

I'll present this in the QBR and include the conservative runway ask plus upside from the hosted experiment so the execs see both the risk and the uplift. Emma — cc'd to keep you in the loop on pilot timing; we'll follow up with a concrete window once Markus confirms the gating checklist.

Thanks all,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: qbr_final_action_items.pdf (slide excerpt)
